This small plot near my house is my main maize field, and I must make it yield well to feed my family and sell a little at the market. I will buy some urea and NPK from the agro-dealer like I do every year, and spread the manure from my goats and few cattle before planting. I cannot afford irrigation here — I depend on the rains like everyone in my village — but I will buy improved maize seed from the dealer because it gives better cobs, and a little herbicide to save my back from weeding this hard soil. My wife, my older children and I will do most of the work, but at planting and weeding time I will call two or three young men from the village for a few days to help me finish on time.
